title: Théorie des cycles algébriques : conjectures de Hodge, Tate, Lefschetz, Weil : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
This is not a Grothendieck manuscript page in the strict sense. It is a typescript page ('- 20 -') of a preliminary version of SGA 4, Exposé V, 'Cohomologie dans les topos' (written up by Verdier from Grothendieck's seminar). Its cross-references (2.4.14.II, 3.5.4.III) point to Exposés II and III of SGA 4. The leaf was evidently reused as scrap paper in the cycles/abelian-varieties dossier, since the neighbouring pages are handwritten notes on the category of abelian varieties. The only manuscript trace on this page is a pencil loop around 'Désignons alors par :'.

Mathematical content.
(i) End of a proof about the Čech-to-derived-functor spectral sequences on a site. The first is indexed by covering sieves R ↪ X. The second is E_2^{p,q} = Ȟ^p(X, ℋ^q(F)) ⇒ H^{p+q}(X, F), interpreted as a composite-functor spectral sequence. The statements about the edge maps Φ^q : Ȟ^q(X,F) → H^q(X,F) (and Φ^q_X) are standard: they are isomorphisms for q = 0, 1 and injective for q = 2. These follow from the vanishing Ȟ^0(ℋ^q(F)) = 0 for q ≠ 0, i.e. the presheaf ℋ^q(F) is locally zero (its sheafification vanishes).
(ii) Corollaire 2.6 (of 2.5). Let E be a topos, A a commutative unital ring object, S an object of E, and F an A-module, with underlying abelian sheaf F̲. The forgetful functor F ↦ F̲ is exact. Hence the identification H^0(E/S, F) ≅ H^0(E/S, F̲) extends to a morphism of δ-functors H^q(E/S, F) → H^q(E/S, F̲), and these maps are isomorphisms. In other words, cohomology computed in A-modules agrees with cohomology computed in abelian sheaves.
(iii) Start of the proof. One reduces to E = sheaves on a U-small site C containing S, with representable fibre products. One then introduces ℋ^0 : C~_A → C^_A, the inclusion of sheaves of A-modules into presheaves of A-modules. The argument presumably continues by computing the derived functors of ℋ^0 via presheaf cohomology (Čech), which does not depend on whether one works with A-modules or abelian groups.
errors: No mathematical errors visible. The proof is only begun on this page, so nothing can be checked beyond the setup.

ideas.what: Čech-to-derived spectral sequence on a site; edge maps Φ^q are isomorphisms for q≤1 and injective for q=2, via vanishing of Ȟ^0(ℋ^q(F)) for q>0

ideas.what: Cohomology of an A-module on a topos agrees with the cohomology of its underlying abelian sheaf
ideas.modern_name: independence of sheaf cohomology from the ring of coefficients
ideas.where_published: SGA 4, Exposé V (corollary on the underlying abelian group)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a typescript page of an SGA 4 Exposé V draft, reused as scrap paper, containing standard results published in SGA 4. It has no connection to the cycle-theoretic notes on the surrounding pages.
transcription_corrections: 'H^0(E.S,F)' should read 'H^0(E/S, F̲)', with F underlined (the underlying abelian group).
In the second morphism the target is H^q(E/S, F̲), with F underlined.
The machine transcription's '$\check{\mathcal{H}}^0$' is a check-H (the Čech presheaf H^0 functor); '$C^\sim_A \to C^\wedge_A$' denotes sheaves versus presheaves of A-modules.
The '76' at the bottom is a handwritten archive folio number; '- 20 -' is the typescript's own page number.
The circled 'Désignons alors par :' is a manuscript pencil mark, not typed text.
